affect

/uh-FEKT/ (verb) · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To affect is to influence someone or something.

Loud noises can affect a person's ability to concentrate.

Example

Researchers track a group of teenagers for a month, recording how long each one sleeps. They find that every lost hour of sleep affects the next day's memory-test scores, dragging them noticeably lower.

Sleep is acting on the test scores — influencing them — which is exactly what the verb affect means. Affect is more precise than 'change' because it emphasizes one thing exerting influence on another, and as a verb it should not be confused with the noun that names the result.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

influence: To influence is to shape someone's actions, thoughts, or decisions, usually gradually and without force. To affect covers any impact at all, sudden or slow, on people or things alike. Influence steers something in a direction; affect simply says that one thing acted on another.

sway: To sway someone is to gently change their opinion or choice -- a closing speech can sway a jury. To affect is broader: it reaches feelings, health, schedules, anything one thing can act on. Sway needs a decision in play; affect does not.

alter: To alter something is to make it become noticeably different -- you can point to what changed. To affect something is to influence it, and that influence may leave no visible mark at all. Alter requires a change you can see or measure; affect does not.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

preserve: keep something unchanged and protected

stabilize: make something steady and resistant to change

Where it sits · how much change it causes — nudge → affect → reshape → transform

nudge vs. affect: Nudge is weaker than affect — to nudge a decision is to push it just slightly, while to affect it is to genuinely influence the outcome.

reshape vs. affect: Reshape is stronger than affect; something that affects your plans influences them, but something that reshapes your plans changes their basic form.

transform vs. affect: Transform is far stronger than affect — a factor that affects a town influences daily life there, while one that transforms the town makes it almost unrecognizable.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — af-

prefix — af-: to, toward (a form of ad-) (Latin)

root — fect

root — fect: to do, make (Latin (facere))

Put it together

Put it together: Af- (toward) + fect (do, make): to affect something is to 'do something to' it — to act on it and influence it.

Use the root in a new word: factory

Use the root in a new word: factory: The factory produces thousands of sneakers every day.

Root Check

Word Choice

Affect is the verb describing an action in progress, usually followed by a direct object (the delay will affect our schedule) — don't confuse it with "effect," the noun taught in this same unit, which names the result that action produces rather than the act of causing it.
